title: Every /rankings page load silently POSTs tep_multiplier=1.15, which bypasses the ADR-015 TE-basis curve — the rendered board under-prices 82 TEs by up to 21.2% and disagrees with GET /api/data on 627 ranks, while every server-side engine keeps pricing from /api/data
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'TE rows from non-TEP sources are lifted onto the basis the board is anchored on via convert_te_value(from_basis="base", to_basis="tepp") — KTC's own measured uplift, 1.209 at the top of the board rising toward 2.05 down it. Replaces a flat 1.15 that sat below the entire observed range.' And frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:2025-2028: 'Default path (no overrides) ... the backend will derive tep_multiplier ... so the frontend doesn't need to POST anything.'
observed: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier = 1.15 is a finite number, and tepMultiplierIsCustomized() returns true for ANY finite number. So `customized` is true on every session including a browser with no localStorage at all. Measured in Chromium after `localStorage.removeItem('next_settings_v2')`: the very first request /rankings makes is POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta with body {"tep_multiplier":1.15}. The backend then sets tep_multiplier_is_override=True (tepMultiplierSource:'override'), and data_contract.py:6939 `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:` skips the te_basis_conversion block entirely — the flag is ON and the curve is loadable, it is simply never entered. Result: the board a user reads is a different board from the one GET /api/data serves and every server-side engine prices from. 8/8 sampled DOM cells reproduce the tep=1.15 delta payload exactly and none reproduce /api/data.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/base-full.json; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/rankings/overrides?view=delta' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tep_multiplier":1.15}' -o /tmp/delta-tep115.json; .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W07/te_divergence.py; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"Brevin Jordan","budgetRemaining":100}'
reproduction.expected: The board rendered on /rankings and the board every engine prices from are the same board; a TE's value is one number site-wide.
reproduction.actual: 135 rows differ in value (82 TE, 50 PICK, 3 other), 627 rows differ in canonicalConsensusRank, 654 in canonicalTierId. Brevin Jordan renders as 1,243 on /rankings (DOM-verified) while /api/waiver/faab-recommend answers resolvedAddValue: 1519.0 for the same player in the same session. Three TEs priced by /api/data (Grant Calcaterra 1340, Josh Oliver 1405, Thomas Fidone 1392) fall out of the rendered board's ranked set entirely and display as value 0.

userImpact: A user opens /rankings, reads a tight-end's value, and trades or bids on it. The number is up to 21% lower than the value the site's own FAAB recommender, trade suggester, arbitrage finder and terminal are using for the same player at the same moment, and nothing on screen says the two disagree — /settings positively asserts the opposite by labelling this state 'Default 1.15x'. The direction is systematic: the flat 1.15 sits below the entire measured TE-basis range, so users sell tight ends cheap.

priorFinding.note: Prior stated the mechanism (default settings force the override path, making ADR-015 unreachable). Independently rediscovered here and extended with runtime proof: browser network capture on a cleared localStorage, DOM-vs-payload identity on 8/8 players, and the cross-surface divergence against a live /api/waiver/faab-recommend response. Also quantifies the collateral 627-row rank and 654-row tier drift the prior finding did not measure.

whatWorks: The backend half is correct and deliberate: an operator-typed tep_multiplier SHOULD bypass a measured curve, and data_contract.py documents exactly that. The delta payload is faithful (0 field mismatches vs view=full across 1,092 rows). The defect is entirely that the frontend sends an operator decision nobody made.
rootCause: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier is the literal 1.15 rather than the null 'auto' sentinel the backend contract defines, and tepMultiplierIsCustomized() cannot distinguish 'the user typed 1.15' from 'this is the shipped default'.
requiredRepair: Set SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier back to null (the documented 'derive from league' sentinel) and drop the readSettings() migration that rewrites null to 1.15; the /settings slider should write a number only on an actual user edit. Then re-verify that a cleared-localStorage load fires no override POST and that /rankings matches GET /api/data row-for-row.
dependencies: Interacts with W07-F002 (the /settings UI labelling) and W07-F008 (the client-side overlay path this also strands).

title: /settings renders the forced TE-premium override as 'Default 1.15x' and its 'Reset to default' button writes the override, so no reachable UI state produces the non-override board
claimUnderTest: settings/page.jsx:246-252 — 'Treat the explicit default value ... as "default" so the UI doesn't render the default as a Custom override.'
observed: tepIsDefault is true for tepMultiplier === 1.15, so the slider prints 'Default 1.15x' and the CustomMixBadge stays quiet — while the wire body carries tep_multiplier: 1.15 and the backend stamps tepMultiplierSource: 'override'. The 'Reset to default' button calls update('tepMultiplier', 1.15), i.e. resetting to default WRITES an explicit override. useSettings.readSettings() additionally coerces a stored null (the real 'auto' sentinel) to 1.15 and sets tepDefaultV3Applied so the coercion is one-way. There is no click path in the product that produces tepMultiplier === null.

reproduction.expected: A session that has never touched the TE slider posts no tep_multiplier, and /settings' 'Default' label describes the board actually being served.
reproduction.actual: With localStorage removed, the first POST is {"tep_multiplier":1.15}; the backend response carries tepMultiplierSource:'override' while tepMultiplierDerived is also 1.15, so the response looks identical to the default path and the UI has no signal that the curve was skipped.

numericProof.formula: UI asserts isDefault iff tepMultiplier === 1.15; backend asserts isOverride iff the key is present

userImpact: A user who wants the platform's designed TE valuation cannot get it, and is told they already have it. Anyone diagnosing the TE discrepancy from the UI is sent the wrong way: both the slider caption and rankingsOverride.isCustomized:false say 'nothing is overridden'.

priorFinding.note: Independently rediscovered. Adds that rankingsOverride.isCustomized comes back false on the override path too, so the backend's own response cannot be used to detect the state either.

whatWorks: tepNativeMultiplier defaults to null and behaves correctly — it is the working shape the tepMultiplier knob should copy.
rootCause: Two different definitions of 'default': the UI's (value equals the shipped constant) and the backend's (key absent).
requiredRepair: Make null the only 'default' state in the UI as well as on the wire; 'Reset to default' should clear the key, not write 1.15.

title: 222 rows on the live board display a client-invented ordinal in the # column, and CLAUDE.md's stated bound for that fallback is factually wrong — the backend's board stops at rank 740, never reaching the 800 limit the doc cites
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'buildRows assigns a display ordinal computedConsensusRank = i + 1 ... and uses it for r.rank only when the backend stamped no canonicalConsensusRank on that row. In practice that is players past the backend's OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT (800) — rows the backend deliberately left unranked.'
observed: On the live 1,092-row contract the deepest backend-stamped rank is 740; OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT (800) is never reached, so the doc's stated population does not exist. The rows that actually take the fallback are the 239 non-pick rows the backend refused to price at all — canonicalConsensusRank null AND rankDerivedValue null AND canonicalTierId null AND confidenceLabel 'None - unranked'. After the rankings page's own filters, 222 of them render with a client-invented # in the range 854-1092. Reproduced in the browser: Austin Ekeler renders '#865', AJ Dillon '#858', Alexander Mattison '#860', Arian Smith '#864' — visually identical to Josh Allen's backend-stamped '#1'. The mechanism claim ('a backend-stamped rank always wins') IS true and was verified: Trey Lance #673 and T.J. Watt #185 reproduce the backend stamp exactly.

reproduction.expected: Rows the backend declined to rank show no rank number (the treatment picks already get: r.rank = null).
reproduction.actual: 222 rows show a fabricated ordinal indistinguishable from a real rank; the deepest is #1092 for a player with no value.

numericProof.formula: fabricated = rows where canonicalConsensusRank is null AND assetClass != 'pick' AND pos is renderable; ordinal = sortIndex + 1 over all materialized rows

userImpact: A user sorting or filtering the deep board reads '#865 Austin Ekeler, RB115' and treats it as the platform's assessment. It is an array index. The board has no opinion on this player at all — the value cell shows 0 — yet the rank cell asserts a precise position among 1,092 assets.

priorFinding.note: Prior counted 216 and framed the ordinals as 'array indices that count unranked picks'. Independently reproduced at 222 on today's contract and refined: picks are correctly excluded from the fallback (r.rank = null for assetClass 'pick'), but they still occupy sort slots so the ordinals skip. The new part is that CLAUDE.md's stated bound for the fallback is measurably false — the 800 limit is never reached and the affected rows are unpriced, not merely deep.

whatWorks: The precedence rule is correct and verified: a backend-stamped canonicalConsensusRank always wins, and picks correctly render no rank. The fail-fast on a payload with zero rank stamps is real code and is reachable.
rootCause: The fallback branch at dynasty-data.js:1402 treats 'backend left this unranked' and 'legacy payload with no stamps' as the same case.
requiredRepair: Give unpriced non-pick rows the same treatment as picks — r.rank = null — and let the # column render the existing '-' placeholder. computedConsensusRank can stay as an internal sort key.
dependencies: W07-F004 depends on this: tierLabel and the positional-rank map are both derived from r.rank.

title: The board fabricates a tier, a positional rank, a confidence badge and an actionable BUY/SELL verdict for the 222 players it declines to price
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'buildRows is a pure materializer ... it trusts backend stamps verbatim.' board-sections.jsx: 'these render backend stamps verbatim (no ranking math client-side).'
observed: For Austin Ekeler the backend stamps canonicalTierId: null, positionRank: null, confidenceLabel: 'None - unranked', confidenceBucket: 'none', marketGapDirection: 'none', edgeSignal: null, rankDerivedValue: null. The rendered row shows TIER 'Tier 10', POS 'RB 115', CONFIDENCE 'Low', VALUE '0'. Alexander Mattison renders EDGE 'SELL' and AJ Dillon renders EDGE 'BUY'. Each is client-computed: tierLabel() falls through to rankBasedTierLabel(row.rank) — a tier derived from the invented ordinal of W07-F003; positionRankByName (page.jsx:716) re-derives QB1/RB115 client-side from the same ordinals; marketAction()/marketEdge() recompute a retail-vs-consensus verdict from effectiveSourceRanks without ever consulting the backend's marketGapDirection.

reproduction.command: PW_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W07/probes/w07_probe2.py  # then: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;c=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W07/base-full.json'));i={p['displayName']:p for p in c['playersArray']};print(i['Austin Ekeler'])"
reproduction.expected: A row the pipeline declined to price shows no tier, no positional rank, no confidence grade and no buy/sell verdict.
reproduction.actual: Rendered: #865 / Tier 10 / RB 115 / Low / '0' / '-' for Ekeler; AJ Dillon renders EDGE 'BUY' and Alexander Mattison EDGE 'SELL' on rows with rankDerivedValue null.

numericProof.formula: tierLabel(row) = canonicalTierId ?? rankBasedTierId(row.rank); row.rank = computedConsensusRank for unpriced rows

userImpact: The board tells a user to BUY a player it has assigned no value, and files him in 'Tier 10' as if that were a modelled cluster. A manager screening for buy-low targets deep on the board is served pure sort-order artefacts as trade advice.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A01-F02/F03 cover contradictory edge thresholds in general. The specific defect here — an actionable BUY/SELL, a tier and a positional rank emitted for rows the backend explicitly refused to price — is new, and it is downstream of PRIOR-A01-F01 (confirmed as W07-F003) rather than a restatement of it.

whatWorks: The VALUE cell is honest-ish for these rows (it renders 0 with a '-' grade rather than inventing a number), and the CONSENSUS cell correctly renders '-'.
rootCause: Every derived display field keys off row.rank, which W07-F003 populates with an invented ordinal; and marketEdge() was written against per-source ranks rather than against the backend's own marketGapDirection stamp.
requiredRepair: Fix W07-F003 first (r.rank = null for unpriced rows) — that alone corrects tier and positional rank. Separately, gate marketAction() on rankDerivedValue being non-null, or key it off the backend's marketGapDirection.

title: The rankings-override delta is 3.74 MB / 342 KB gzipped, not the ~1.25 MB / ~100 KB CLAUDE.md documents, and W07-F001 puts that POST on the critical path of every page load for every user
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Production payload drops from ~4 MB to ~1.25 MB uncompressed, and to ~100 KB over the wire with FastAPI's GZipMiddleware.'
observed: Measured on the live 1,092-row contract: view=full is 11,271,885 bytes and view=delta is 3,739,098 bytes (ratio 0.332), gzipped over the wire 349,679 bytes. Both documented absolute figures are understated ~3x. 2.20 MB of the 3.74 MB delta — 59% — is the sourceRankMeta block, shipped for all 1,092 rows on every request. The pinning test (test_delta_byte_size_is_bounded) asserts delta_bytes < 55,000 against a toy fixture and delta/full < 0.60, so neither production absolute size nor a 3x drift trips it. This matters more than doc drift because W07-F001 makes this POST fire on every page load of every session, so it is no longer a customized-session cost.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/rankings/overrides?view=delta' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' -d '{"tep_multiplier":1.15}' -o /tmp/gz.bin -w 'wire=%{size_download}\n'; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/rankings/overrides?view=full' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tep_multiplier":1.15}' -o /tmp/full.json -w 'full=%{size_download}\n'
reproduction.expected: delta ~1,250,000 bytes uncompressed, ~100,000 bytes on the wire
reproduction.actual: delta 3,739,098 bytes uncompressed, 349,679 bytes on the wire; full 11,271,885 bytes

numericProof.formula: ratio = deltaBytes / fullBytes; documented_error = deltaBytes / documentedDeltaBytes

userImpact: Every navigation to any contract-consuming page pays a 350 KB compressed download plus a full backend re-run of the ranking pipeline, in addition to the base contract fetch. On a slow connection the board is the last thing to settle.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding in areas 1 or 6 covers the override payload's measured size.

whatWorks: The delta itself is correct: across 1,092 rows and the fields rankDerivedValue / canonicalConsensusRank / canonicalTierId / confidence, the delta and the full contract agree on every single row (0 mismatches, 0 rows present in one and not the other). GZipMiddleware is active (content-encoding: gzip confirmed).
rootCause: sourceRankMeta is in _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS because it is override-sensitive, but it is only READ by the expanded per-row source-audit panel — one row at a time, on demand.
requiredRepair: Either drop sourceRankMeta from the delta and fetch it per-row when a user expands the audit panel, or re-state the documented sizes with the measured ones and add a production-scale assertion to test_delta_byte_size_is_bounded so the next 3x drift is caught.

title: The client-side league-adjusted overlay path (_fetchValuationOverlay + applyValuationOverlay + GET /api/valuation/league-adjusted) is unreachable in the running product — the lens is served entirely server-side because W07-F001 makes every session 'customized'
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'the valuation overlay ... is an overlay the client applies, never contract fields' and useSettings.js:88 '"leagueAdjusted" overlays GET /api/valuation/league-adjusted'.
observed: That branch runs only when `customized` is false, which W07-F001 makes impossible. Network capture of a real toggle click on /rankings (localStorage cleared beforehand) shows the only requests fired are POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta with {"tep_multiplier":1.15,"valuation_mode":"leagueAdjusted"} and GET /api/terminal?valuationMode=leagueAdjusted — no GET /api/valuation/league-adjusted at all. dynasty-data.js:1851 is the endpoint's only caller in the frontend. So ~150 lines of merge logic and its regression suite guard a path no user reaches, and the endpoint is live but unconsumed by the page it was built for.

reproduction.expected: Toggling 'My league' on /rankings fetches the overlay endpoint.
reproduction.actual: No overlay request is made; the lens rides the override POST and is composed server-side.

numericProof.formula: count of GET /api/valuation/league-adjusted in the network log after clicking 'My league'

userImpact: None directly — the server-side composition is the more correct of the two paths. The cost is maintenance risk: a whole tested code path that cannot regress visibly, and a documented mechanism that does not describe the running system.

priorFinding.note: Not covered by any prior finding in areas 1 or 6.

whatWorks: The server-side composition path is correct and verified end to end (see W07-F007). GET /api/valuation/league-adjusted itself answers 200 with 709 factors / 740 ranks / 740 tiers and isNoop:false.
rootCause: Consequence of W07-F001 — `customized` is unconditionally true.
requiredRepair: After fixing W07-F001 this path becomes live again for default sessions; decide deliberately whether to keep it or route everything through the server-side composition and delete it.

title: Verified working: source toggles and weight edits on /settings change displayed values end to end; the valuation-mode toggle persists across reload and navigation and reaches the engines; CSV export matches the screen; the live source registry is in parity
claimUnderTest: A 2026-07-29 audit found the /settings sliders inert. CLAUDE.md claims the override flow reaches the same canonical pipeline, that the mode toggle reaches every engine, and that caches key on the mode.
observed: All four claims hold under runtime test. (1) Unchecking 'Include KeepTradeCut SF-TE++ in blend' in the real /settings UI writes {"ktcSfTep":{"include":false}} to localStorage, fires POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta with {"ktcSfTep":{"include":false},"tep_multiplier":1.15}, and the /rankings board changes visibly: Josh Allen 9,988 -> 9,987, Brock Bowers 9,876 -> 9,878, and the #4 slot flips from Ja'Marr Chase to Drake Maye. Server-side the same body moves 491 of 1,092 values and 582 ranks; disabling idpTradeCalc moves 782 values; setting dlfSf weight 3.0 moves 222. The sliders are not inert. (2) Clicking 'My league' writes valuationMode:'leagueAdjusted', which survives a full page reload and an SPA navigation to /trade and back; every subsequent engine request carries it (POST override body valuation_mode, GET /api/terminal?valuationMode=leagueAdjusted). The override memo keys on JSON.stringify(body), and body carries valuation_mode, so the cache cannot serve a stale market board. (3) CSV export emits exactly the 200 displayed player rows (the 230 tbody <tr> are 200 players + 30 tier dividers), in the on-screen order, from the same displayRows array the table renders, and stamps a 'Value Basis' column per row. (4) GET /api/rankings/sources returns 21 sources matching frontend RANKING_SOURCES key-for-key AND in the same order; tests/api/test_source_registry_parity.py + test_source_overrides.py pass 82/82 on .venv python 3.11.15.

reproduction.command: PW_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W07/probes/w07_probe6.py && PW_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/.venv/bin/python w07_probe5.py && cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/api/test_source_registry_parity.py tests/api/test_source_overrides.py -q
reproduction.expected: Toggling a source changes rendered values; the mode persists and reaches engines; export == screen; registries agree.

numericProof.formula: csvDataRows == screenPlayerRows; set(backendKeys) == set(frontendKeys) and order equal

userImpact: None — this is the working half.

priorFinding.note: The 2026-07-29 'sliders are inert' defect named in the workstream brief does not reproduce: a real UI checkbox interaction round-trips to a changed rendered value. Recording the negative result rather than hiding it.

title: Under the league-adjusted lens the board breaks its own documented 0-9999 ceiling — Josh Allen renders 10,171
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Common 0-9999 internal value scale' and 'Both top out at 9999, so there is no rescaling to apply between them.'
observed: Switching the Value basis to 'My league' renders Josh Allen at 10,171, Bijan Robinson at 10,109 and Brock Bowers at 9,991 — the scarcity factor is a plain multiply with no post-multiply renormalisation, so the top of the board exits the declared scale. Value bands ('S+') and any downstream consumer that assumes a 9,999 ceiling now see out-of-range inputs. Measured factors range up to 1.098 (Abdul Carter) on 709 of 1,092 rows.
userImpact: Minor: a user comparing an adjusted number against any other surface's 0-9999 number (a KTC value, an exported CSV from market mode) is comparing different scales without being told.

priorFinding.note: Not covered by any prior finding in areas 1 or 6.

whatWorks: The overlay is otherwise coherent: ranks are backend-computed and dense (740 of them), factors are position-only so they compose against a re-weighted board, and the toggle correctly re-ranks (Bijan Robinson moves 3 -> 2 past Brock Bowers).
rootCause: overlay.adjusted_rows multiplies without clamping or renormalising to the scale maximum.
requiredRepair: Either clamp/renormalise the adjusted board to 9,999 or state explicitly in the contract and the UI that the adjusted scale is unbounded above.

title: Confirmed: the desktop rankings path requests view=array, so the legacy players-dict materializer CLAUDE.md calls the default path is not the live one
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md's valuation-overlay section: 'the legacy dict uses _canonicalConsensusRank but rankDerivedValue, and the legacy path is the default one.'
observed: Browser network capture shows the live desktop request is GET /api/dynasty-data?view=array. buildRows takes the playersArray branch whenever playersArray is non-empty, and the array branch is what every desktop session gets. The legacy-dict branch is still exercised by the view=app compact payload (which genuinely has no playersArray — verified: GET /api/data?view=app returns a 1,092-entry players dict and no playersArray key), so it is live but not default.

reproduction.command: PW_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W07/probes/w07_probe5.py  # see tradeRequests; and: curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data?view=app' | .venv/bin/python -c "import sys,json;print('playersArray' in json.load(sys.stdin))"
reproduction.expected: Desktop takes the legacy players-dict path per the docs.
reproduction.actual: Desktop requests view=array and takes the playersArray path; view=app (mobile) has no playersArray and is the only live consumer of the legacy branch.

numericProof.formula: buildRows uses playersArray branch iff Array.isArray(data.playersArray) && length > 0

userImpact: Documentation-only for now, but it directs anyone debugging a rankings display bug to the wrong materializer, and the two branches do not stamp identical field sets.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced by network capture rather than by reading code; adds the measured confirmation that view=app genuinely carries no playersArray key, so the legacy branch is live for mobile rather than dead.

whatWorks: Both branches produce backend-stamped ranks and values; the parity between them was not exhaustively diffed in this workstream.
rootCause: Doc drift after the view=array default landed.
requiredRepair: Correct the CLAUDE.md sentence; state that view=array is the desktop default and the legacy dict serves view=app.
